The mask is stored as a plain tensor attribute rather than a registered buffer, so `.to('cuda')` leaves it on CPU; the code path that hits it raises a device error only for long sequences, or worse, a broadcast silently produces a mask of the wrong shape that masks nothing.

Sampling is done from the logits at all T positions, or the context is never cropped to block_size, so generation is fine for the first block_size tokens and then either crashes on the positional embedding lookup or wraps around and produces nonsense - the training run is blamed for a decoding bug.

Val loss is compared against a published number from a model with a different tokenizer; per-token cross-entropy is not comparable across vocabularies, so the write-up claims a result it has not earned - the fix is bits-per-byte, and nobody notices until a reviewer asks.

Derive DPO starting from the KL-regularised RL objective and the Bradley-Terry model. Where does the partition function go and why is that the key step? What does beta control, and what does the per-pair gradient weight look like?

A customer has one 24 GB GPU, a 7B base model and 12,000 labelled examples. Do the memory arithmetic for full fine-tune, LoRA and QLoRA in bytes per parameter, tell me what you would run, and defend your r, lora_alpha, target_modules and learning rate.

Write the LoRA forward pass and its parameter count. Why is B initialised to zero? Why does the alpha/r scaling exist and what does rsLoRA change about it? What exactly goes wrong if you merge the adapter into a 4-bit base?

Debug: a DPO run reports rewards/accuracies of 0.93, steadily rising rewards/margins, and a 58% win rate against base judged by a strong LLM. The customer says the model got worse. What do you check, in what order, and what would convince you either way?
Debug: a QLoRA run's training loss is flat from step 0 and never moves. Give me five distinct causes and how you would distinguish them in under twenty minutes.

Design the evaluation you would put in front of the customer's VP to justify shipping a fine-tune. Which datasets, which metrics, which statistics, how you control judge bias, and what result would make you recommend against shipping.

When do you tell a customer that fine-tuning is the wrong tool? Name the signals in their request that trigger that call, and say what you would propose instead and how you would prove it was the better choice.

Eval rows were paraphrases of training rows from the same tickets and the split was random rather than grouped by ticket id; the tuned model scores 18 points above base on the held-out set and is worse than base on genuinely new tickets in week one of the pilot.

Labels were never masked to -100 over the prompt, so the loss rewards reproducing the system prompt; train loss looks excellent, and the deployed model starts answering by restating the instructions before it gets to the customer's question.

target_modules named the wrong projections for the architecture, so few or no modules matched; print_trainable_parameters was never read, the run trained a fraction of what was intended, and the team concluded 'LoRA does not work for this task' and quoted a full fine-tune.

LoRA was launched with the full fine-tune learning rate of 2e-5 instead of 2e-4; the loss barely moves over three epochs and the result is presented as evidence that the base model cannot learn the task.

Gradient checkpointing was enabled on a frozen 4-bit base without prepare_model_for_kbit_training or enable_input_require_grads, so no input required grad, the adapters received no gradient, and a perfectly flat loss curve was debugged for two days as a data-quality problem.

DPO drove rewards/accuracies to 0.95 while mean completion length doubled; the LLM judge, which prefers longer answers, reported a 68% win rate, and the customer's support team complained the assistant now waffles - the entire gain was length.

The adapter was merged into the 4-bit quantized base for serving and evaluation was never rerun; the dequantize-merge-requantize round trip cost several points that showed up only as user complaints about the production model being worse than the demo.

Base was evaluated greedily while the tuned model was sampled at temperature 0.8 with no fixed seed, so run-to-run noise of plus or minus 4 points swamped the claimed 3-point improvement, and the gain vanished when the customer reran the script.

Write the symmetric InfoNCE loss for a batch of N image-text pairs from memory, then derive the gradient with respect to the logits. Why is the loss log N at initialisation, and what exactly does the learned temperature do to that gradient as it goes to zero and as it grows?

A customer's text-to-image demo returns plausible but wrong images. Walk me through your diagnosis in order: what do you measure to distinguish too-few-negatives, false negatives in the batch, hubness or representation collapse, and the modality gap - and what single plot do you put in front of them?

Why is contrastive batch size a property of the objective rather than an infrastructure detail? State the bound it relates to, then give me three ways to get 32k negatives on four GPUs and tell me what each one costs in compute, staleness or correctness.

Explain the modality gap: where does it come from, why does contrastive training not close it, and name one concrete production decision it changes. How would you measure it on a checkpoint you were handed this morning?

SigLIP replaces the batch softmax with a per-pair sigmoid. Write both losses, explain what changes under data parallelism, why the bias term is initialised strongly negative, and when you would still choose softmax InfoNCE.

Design: 40,000 product photos, a one-line merchandiser description each, no labels, one A10, and the customer wants natural-language search live in three weeks. Zero-shot pretrained, locked-image tuning, or train from scratch? Name the eval you would agree with them up front, and say what you would do if R@1 came back at 12 percent.

CLIP scores 'a horse eating grass' and 'grass eating a horse' almost identically. Explain why the training objective permits this, how you would measure it on the customer's own query distribution, and what you would change in training or in the serving architecture to fix it.

The Dataset yields one row per (image, caption) on Flickr8k, so up to five true partners for the same image land in one batch and the loss actively pushes correct pairs apart; training converges, the curve looks textbook, and R@1 sits several points below where it should for reasons no learning-rate sweep will find.

F.normalize is omitted on one tower (or applied before the projection instead of after), so the loss can be reduced by growing embedding norms rather than by aligning pairs; the loss falls smoothly, the temperature stops meaning anything, and the retrieval index ranks by magnitude.

logit_scale is left learnable but unclamped, runs past 100 on an easy batch, the softmax saturates and the run NaNs under fp16 at epoch three - which is then debugged for a day as a corrupt-image problem in the dataloader.

Multi-GPU training gathers embeddings with a plain torch.distributed.all_gather and overwrites the local slice, so gradients flow for only one rank's share of the negatives; the 8-GPU run reaches exactly the 1-GPU quality at 8x the cost and the team concludes 'contrastive scaling does not work for us'.

Image-to-text R@K is computed with the any-of-five-captions convention and text-to-image with the one-correct-image convention, then the two are quoted side by side as if symmetric, or the model's R@1 on a 1000-image gallery is compared to a published R@1 on 5000 - the headline number is roughly double what it should be and the customer's own test reproduces none of it.

Zero-shot CIFAR-10 is evaluated with the raw label 'plane' and no prompt template, comes in ten points below the published baseline, and the gap is attributed to the training run rather than to the prompt - so a week is spent tuning a model that was never the problem.

A similarity threshold of 0.5, copied from a sentence-embedding service, is used to decide whether a retrieved image is a match; the modality gap puts true image-caption pairs at 0.25 and unrelated image-image pairs at 0.75, so the system rejects every correct result while confidently deduplicating distinct products.

The whole dual encoder is fine-tuned on the customer's 3,000 in-domain pairs with no weight-space ensembling and no frozen zero-shot regression suite in CI; the pilot category improves, every other category silently degrades, and the failure surfaces two months later as 'the model got worse after your update'.

Derive the GCN layer from the spectral formulation: start at L_sym = I - D^-1/2 A D^-1/2, take the first-order Chebyshev approximation, and get to D~^-1/2 A~ D~^-1/2 H W. Then tell me exactly what the renormalisation trick buys you and what goes wrong with plain mean aggregation instead.

Implement a GCN layer on a whiteboard given only edge_index of shape (2, E) and a feature matrix X, with no library layers. Where does the degree normalisation come from, what happens to a node of degree zero, and how would you change your code to make it a GAT layer?

A customer's GCN gets 79 percent at two layers, 76 at four and 41 at eight. Walk me through how you decide whether this is over-smoothing, over-squashing, vanishing gradients or overfitting. What do you measure, what plot do you produce, and what is the fix in each case?

Design: a bank gives you accounts, users, transactions and products across four tables, and wants to flag accounts likely to be mules within the next 30 days. Define the graph, the task level, the label and its timestamp, the split, the metric, the baselines you must beat, and whether you would reach for GCN, GraphSAGE, GAT or R-GCN - and why you rejected the other three.

Explain why a message-passing GNN is bounded by the 1-WL test. Give me two non-isomorphic graphs it cannot tell apart, and tell me what that implies for detecting a circular-payment ring - including what you would add to the input to make the pattern learnable.

Your team reports 0.99 ROC-AUC on link prediction for a product recommender and it performs at chance in the pilot. List the three most likely causes in order, say how you would test each in under an hour, and describe the evaluation protocol you would have insisted on instead.

The customer's graph has 40 million edges and will not fit in GPU memory full-batch. Compare neighbour sampling, Cluster-GCN and GraphSAINT: what bias does each introduce, how does each interact with the depth you need, and what has to change at inference time so that serving matches training?

deg.pow(-0.5) is applied without masking degree-zero nodes, so isolated accounts in the customer extract produce inf, the scatter turns inf*0 into NaN, the loss is NaN by the second epoch, and three hours go into lowering the learning rate before anyone prints the degree histogram.

The customer's undirected relationship table is loaded into edge_index in one direction only; message passing is silently directed, half the neighbourhood never contributes, accuracy sits four to six points below the published number, and it gets debugged as a hyperparameter problem for a week.

GAT's softmax is computed over all E edges instead of segmented by destination node; the code runs, the loss decreases, the attention coefficients sum to one across the entire graph rather than per neighbourhood, and the model quietly degenerates to a degree-weighted average.

Link prediction is evaluated with positive supervision edges still present in the adjacency used for message passing; the model reads the label off its own input, offline ROC-AUC is 0.99, and the deployed recommender performs at chance.

A fraud graph is split uniformly at random rather than by time, so message passing at training time aggregates transactions that had not happened yet; PR-AUC on the holdout is excellent, the live model catches nothing, and the postmortem blames data drift rather than the split.

A two-layer GCN reports 98 percent accuracy on a 2-percent-positive AML graph and is presented as a success; a constant predict-licit baseline scores 98 percent too, and nobody computed precision and recall on the illicit class.

Depth-versus-accuracy falls off after three layers, the team reads it as overfitting and increases dropout and weight decay; training accuracy is also falling because the representations are over-smoothed, so the regularisation makes it strictly worse and the real fix - fewer layers plus a jumping-knowledge or residual path - is never tried.

Cluster-GCN with METIS partitioning trains on intra-cluster edges only while inference uses full neighbourhoods, so the serving-time aggregation is over a distribution the model never saw; the offline validation number was computed on the same truncated graph and did not catch it.

A GAT attention heat map is shown to a customer's analysts as evidence that the model focuses on a particular counterparty; the weights are from one head of one layer, are not identifiable, and by the GATv2 static-attention result the same neighbour may be ranked top for every node in the graph.
